heading: 2026.03.22 — Boss Fight~C verifier-bundle card cutover and reopen ladder (no publication)
subject: tighter replayable-verifier stop rules for same-number / different-checker drift and explicit reopen ownership in Boss Fight~C
state_before: Boss Fight~C already exposed the replayable verifier bundle, the minimal public verifier-bundle card, and a tiny checker drill, but the smallest quotable cutover between reusing the same local arithmetic and reusing the same public verifier contract still lived mostly in operator inference, especially when the checker version, declared plan schema, or declared dual schema changed while the replayed numbers stayed fixed
state_after: Boss Fight~C now adds a compact fail-closed verifier-bundle cutover drill showing that reusing the same $p=0.041$, $d=0.047$, and $B=0.050$ values still licenses the old public card only while the declared plan schema, dual schema, and checker version remain `bf-plan-v1` / `bf-dual-v1` / `bf-checker-v1`, makes explicit that switching to `bf-checker-v2` or changing the declared schema identifiers forces a new verifier-bundle card even before any higher-layer notarization or release packaging is discussed, states that a changed published cap is already a Boss Fight~A / Boss Fight~B widening rather than a mere verifier refresh, adds a minimal reopen ladder naming Boss Fight~A / Boss Fight~B / the Boss Fight~B addendum / Eval~1 / ABOM-OINL / Release~A, refreshes the published-ready note accordingly, compiles cleanly in scratch LaTeX checks, and leaves the queue posture unchanged
reason: the archive is easier to audit when the verifier-bundle paper itself states exactly what the old public card still licenses a later terse paper to say, and when it makes the fail-closed boundary between ``same replayed arithmetic'' and ``same declared replay contract'' explicit instead of delegating that cutover to neighboring papers or operator memory
follow_up_needed: keep Boss Fight~C in published_ready without publishing it yet; future passes can now tighten Eval~1, Anonymity~C, Release~A, or the Boss Fight~B addendum against this clearer verifier-bundle boundary instead of re-explaining where the old public replay contract stops
summary: This drafting pass tightens the replayable verifier-bundle companion itself rather than widening the repeated-use accountant root, the practical anonymous-DHT dial sheet, the optional evidence-table addendum, the evaluator-notarization layer, the claim-object dossier, or the release-lineage receipts. The goal is to let later terse Anonymous-DHT papers cite one exact verdict about when the same public verifier-bundle card still names the live replay contract, when reusing the same primal/dual numbers after checker-version or schema drift forces a new card, and which neighboring paper owns the next widening step. The pass does not change publication state.
